At the edge of the city, where the last bus turns around, there’s a little patch of grass that no one planned.

In spring, dandelions arrive first. Then clover. Then one day, a sunflower appears—tall, bright, and slightly ridiculous beside the road. No one knows who planted it. The bus driver says it wasn’t there yesterday. A child insists it must have followed the sun all the way from somewhere else.

People begin to look for it on their way home. They don’t stop, exactly. They just turn their heads as the bus swings around.

By August, the sunflower is gone. Its stalk leans into the grass, and the seeds are scattered to the wind. The patch looks ordinary again.

But the next spring, there are three.
